working_title: Breeding-component concentration recurs across spatial scales in Antarctic penguins
central_claim: Non-proportional concentration is strongly replicated during decline within Palmer/Signy breeding systems. At the MAPPPD regional scale, abundance-linked concentration recurs within the declining subset, but all three increasing networks also end with lower effective breeding-site number; regional concentration is therefore not uniquely tied to negative population trend.

evidence_order.scope: three island-based Palmer Adelie sample-colony monitoring networks
species x published APBP region monitored site networks

primary_narrative: within-system concentration exceeds proportional thinning in five declining Palmer/Signy monitored trajectories
the Signy results provide prospective geographic and cross-species replication of concentration during decline
all four declining MAPPPD regional networks have positive calibrated abundance-linked concentration effects, with two individually supported
all three increasing MAPPPD regional networks also end with lower E, including two with increasing N and decreasing E
regional concentration therefore constrains rather than simply extends a decline-specific interpretation
Palmer sample-colony networks and Signy panels show different component-level routes to the same local concentration endpoint
secondary_descriptive_context: the local abundance-E relationship is stronger over long trajectories than first differences
effective component number recovered in only 8/31 local annual abundance rebounds
the frozen local ratchet criterion failed and no regional trend-asymmetry test was prespecified
prohibited_claims: formal regional hysteresis or irreversible ratchet
preferential survival of initially largest components as a universal mechanism
closed demographic population interpretation of APBP regions
causal attribution to snow, site fidelity, dispersal, recruitment or predation
regional concentration is specific to population decline
trend-independent concentration law from the seven MAPPPD panels
negative kappa is evidence against concentration in increasing systems
Palmer summed monitored-component abundance equals complete island population abundance
Palmer colony-code components exhaust physical island breeding space

stop_rule: No further geographic clustering, completeness thresholds, scaling families, lags, trait screens, or same-data mechanism searches are authorized to strengthen the cross-scale claim. New generality requires an independent taxonomic data source.
